The cut is a triangle. When I unfold the paper along the horizontal fold line (which was the bottom edge of the folded square), this triangular cut will be mirrored upwards, creating another triangle on the other side of the center. The net result of this single triangular cut at the center point is a **diamond shape** perfectly centered on the original paper.

So, I expect to see **two horizontal rectangular holes**, one positioned above the center and one below, both perfectly aligned along the vertical centerline of the original paper.

3.  **The top-right corner cut:** This cut is made at the top-right corner of the folded square. This corner, as I noted, represents the **bundle of all four original outer corners** of the paper. The cut is a triangle. When I unfold it, this triangular cut will appear at each of the four original corners of the large square. Essentially, all four corners of the original paper will be **chamfered or clipped diagonally**.

Finally, I'll systematically compare these predicted features with the provided options (A, B, C, D, E).

*   **Rectangular cuts (vertical centerline):** Now, looking at C, D, and E, I need to see which one has the two horizontal rectangles centered on the vertical fold line.
    *   Option C has four small rectangles, but they don't appear to be centered on the vertical line, and there are too many. It's out.
    *   Options D and E both have two rectangular cuts that look like they're centered on the vertical line. So, the distinction must lie elsewhere.
*   **Corner feature (chamfered corners):** Now I compare D and E for the corner cuts.
    *   Option D shows intact square corners. This contradicts my analysis of the top-right corner cut on the folded paper. Option D is eliminated.
    *   Option E clearly shows all four outer corners of the original square with diagonal cuts, exactly as I predicted.

Therefore, based on the cumulative evidence from each cut, option **E** is the only one that perfectly matches the expected outcome of unfolding the paper with the described folds and cuts.

   - The **bottom-left corner** of the folded square corresponds to the exact **center** of the original paper.
   - The **top-right corner** of the folded square corresponds to all **four outer corners** of the original paper folded together.
   - The **left dashed edge** corresponds to the **vertical center line** of the original paper.

2. **Analyze the Cuts (shaded in grey):**
   - **Bottom-left corner cut:** A diagonal cut is made at the center point. When unfolded across both the vertical and horizontal fold lines, this triangle reflects into all four quadrants to form a **diamond shape** in the very center of the paper. *(This eliminates A and B).*
   - **Left-edge cut:** A small rectangular cut is made directly on the vertical fold line. When unfolded horizontally, the two halves join to make a wider rectangle centered on the vertical dashed line. Since the paper was also folded vertically, this creates **two rectangles** (one in the top half, one in the bottom half) sitting directly on the vertical fold line. *(This eliminates C).*
   - **Top-right corner cut:** A diagonal cut is made at the outer corner. Because all four corners of the original square are folded together at this point, unfolding the paper will result in **all four outer corners being cut off diagonally**. *(This eliminates D).*

Matching all three features gives picture **(E)**.
